messages:
maria_support: Customer reporting SSE stream cuts out part-way through a long generation. Request ID: req_8f7a3c. Happens only behind their corporate proxy. Can we get a minimal curl repro + what to collect for a debug bundle?

jon-eng: Can you paste the exact curl they used and the short client trace? Even a one-liner is fine. Also confirm if they use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 via the proxy.

maria_support: Here is what they sent (redacted token):
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***\" \\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\n  -H \"x-request-id: req_8f7a3c\" \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=tts
```
They attached a tiny clip of the output showing a clean stream for ~35s then EOF.

jon-eng: Ok — common failure modes: proxy closing idle keep-alive, incorrect chunked framing, or auth rotation. For a minimal repro we usually ask them to run curl with explicit options to avoid buffering and force HTTP/1.1. Try this and paste the full verbatim output (use a placeholder token):

```
# minimal streaming repro to collect headers & raw bytes
curl -v --http1.1 -N --no-buffer \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\n  -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" \\n  -H \"x-request-id: req_8f7a3c\" \\n  --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt \\n  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=tts&prompt=hello\"
```

jon-eng: Notes: --http1.1 helps with proxies that mishandle h2 upgrade, -N/--no-buffer prevents libcurl buffering which hides chunk boundaries, and --trace-ascii captures the raw bytes for us to inspect.

sam-sre: Also request these items in the debug bundle:
- curl_trace.txt (from --trace-ascii)
- full stdout/stderr from curl run (pastebin or attach)
- client system time + timezone
- proxy vendor/version (e.g., F5, Bluecoat) and any upstream LB in front of the proxy
- packet capture (pcap) while running the curl test (filter by host and req_8f7a3c)
- server-side logs (we'll pull traces once we have req_8f7a3c)

infra-bot: Server traces for req_8f7a3c: logs/streams/2026/03/17/req_8f7a3c.log uploaded to internal debug bucket (redacted link).

carla: Customer ran the suggested curl. Attaching truncated curl_trace.txt (small excerpt):
```
> GET /v1/streams?model=tts&prompt=hello HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
> Accept: text/event-stream
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {\"token\":\"first chunk\"}

... (many chunks) ...

# then at ~37.12s client gets EOF (no final event)
```

jon-eng: From that excerpt it looks like the proxy is terminating the connection mid-stream. Two quick checks for customer to try: 1) run same curl but add header `Connection: close` to see if proxy keepalive handling is the issue; 2) run curl with `--tcp-nodelay` and capture pcap. Also try `--keepalive-time 2` to force kernel keepalive probes (if their curl supports it).

maria_support: Sent those two variations and the pcap request. Asked them to upload curl_trace.txt + pcap + full stdout to our secure upload and to DM the link.

customer-ops: I'll collect the pcap and upload. FYI their proxy is Palo Alto PAN-OS 10.2. I suspect an idle timeout of ~30s.

sam-sre: If proxy idle timeout is the culprit we can recommend enabling small heartbeat SSE events from the client or shorten server-side chunk interval. For immediate diagnostics, the pcap + curl_trace will confirm which side closed first.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll follow up once uploads land and paste server trace snippets. :thumbsup:

jon-eng: If we confirm proxy closed first, recommend either: short-term client heartbeats, or long-term: explicit TLS keepalive config on their proxy or move streaming traffic to a whitelisted egress with longer timeouts.

customer-ops: Upload complete — link in DM. Will update here with timestamps.

maria_support: Acked. Marking this thread for on-call if we need deeper packet analysis.

sam-sre: ping jon-eng if you want me to correlate pcaps with server-side FIN/RST timings.

maria_support: Will do. Thanks all.
